categories.main_business_segments: Electronic Arts (EA) operates as a single reportable segment focused on developing, publishing, and delivering digital interactive entertainment. Its primary business lines include full games (digital downloads and packaged goods), live services (extra content, subscriptions, and in-game purchases), and licensing of games and content to third parties. Key franchises include EA SPORTS FC, Madden NFL, Apex Legends, Battlefield, and The Sims.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: EA leverages proprietary and licensed technologies to develop games for consoles, PCs, and mobile devices. The company emphasizes live services infrastructure, digital distribution, and advanced game engines. EA is investing in artificial intelligence to accelerate production and enable new player experiences, and maintains robust quality controls and cybersecurity measures to support its complex, online-enabled software products.
categories.primary_customers_markets: EA's primary customers are individual gamers who access its products via consoles, PCs, and mobile devices. The company serves a global consumer base, with significant sales through digital storefronts (Sony PlayStation, Microsoft Xbox, Apple App Store, Google Play) and retail partners. Major end markets include sports gaming, action, simulation, and online multiplayer genres.
categories.geographic_coverage: EA operates globally, with 59% of net revenue in FY2025 derived from international markets and 41% from North America. The company’s Swiss entity accounts for a significant portion of international revenue, and key markets include the United States, Europe, and Asia. EA employs approximately 14,500 people worldwide, with 68% located internationally.
categories.supply_chain_position: EA is positioned downstream in the supply chain as a developer, publisher, and distributor of digital interactive entertainment. It relies on upstream partners for platform access (Sony, Microsoft, Apple, Google) and content licenses (sports leagues, IP holders), while distributing directly to consumers and through digital and retail channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: EA’s strategic priorities include expanding live services, deepening player engagement through interactive storytelling and key IP, and growing global online communities around its franchises. The company is investing in artificial intelligence, new business models (such as free-to-play and subscriptions), and innovation in game development and delivery. R&D spending increased 6% in FY2025, reflecting continued investment in studios and technology.
categories.revenue_model: EA generates revenue through a mix of full game sales (digital and physical), live services (in-game purchases, extra content, and subscriptions), and licensing arrangements. Live services, including Ultimate Team extra content, account for 73% of total net revenue. Subscription offerings (EA Play, EA Play Pro) and free-to-play models also contribute to recurring revenue streams.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: EA faces intense competition from established interactive entertainment companies (such as Activision Blizzard, Take-Two Interactive, Ubisoft), large diversified technology firms, and new market entrants. The company is a global leader in sports gaming and maintains strong positions in action, simulation, and online multiplayer genres. EA’s market position is supported by its portfolio of popular franchises and extensive player network.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2025, EA reported $7.5 billion in net revenue, $1.1 billion in net income, and $2.1 billion in operating cash flow. The company experienced a slight revenue decline of 1% year-over-year, with live services revenue also down 2%. EA maintains a strong balance sheet with $2.2 billion in cash and short-term investments, and continues to return capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: EA differentiates itself through its portfolio of high-quality, innovative games and live services, leveraging both owned and licensed IP to create engaging, community-driven experiences. The company emphasizes the value of live services that extend gameplay, the strength of its global player network, and its ability to deliver content across multiple platforms and business models. EA’s focus on interactive storytelling, technological innovation, and player engagement underpins its competitive advantage.
